**Google Business Profile (GBP) signals** remain the most influential factor for local search in 2026, accounting for approximately **32% of total ranking weight** [1-3]. According to the **Whitespark 2026 Local Search Ranking Factors survey**, the single most important individual signal is selecting the most specific **primary category** for your business [4-6]. Following Google's March 2026 core update, **GBP completeness** has shifted from a best practice to an active ranking input; profiles missing hours, service menus, or attributes now face measurable **ranking suppression** [7, 8]. 

**Local Map Pack Ranking Factors**
Google continues to rank the "Local 3-Pack" based on the three pillars of **relevance, distance, and prominence** [1, 5, 9, 10]. 
*   **Relevance:** Determined by category matching and keyword-rich business descriptions (750 characters max) [11-13]. 
*   **Distance:** Highly personalized in 2026; a user 0.5 miles away will see a different pack than one 2 miles away [14, 15]. 
*   **Prominence:** Now heavily weighted toward **real-world engagement**, including brand searches, direction requests, and clicks-to-call, which account for roughly **8% of the algorithm** [2, 16, 17]. 
*   **"Business is Open":** A significant 2026 shift identifies **"open at time of search"** as a top-5 ranking factor; businesses with inaccurate hours lose visibility the moment they are marked "closed" in the system [6, 17, 18].

**Reviews and Review Velocity**
Reviews contribute **16% to 20%** of map pack ranking weight depending on the vendor study [1, 2]. 
*   **Review Velocity:** The 2026 "sweet spot" for most mid-sized markets is generating **1–2 new reviews per week** [19-21]. Sudden spikes in volume are flagged by AI-driven spam filters [20, 22].
*   **AI Citation Threshold:** Vendor research from **ClickRank** identifies a threshold of **150+ reviews per location** as necessary for a business to be reliably recommended by AI assistants like ChatGPT and Gemini [23-25].
*   **Recency and Responses:** Post-March 2026 data shows that reviews from the last **90 days** carry more weight than historical volume [26, 27]. Responding to both positive and negative reviews within **24–48 hours** is now a confirmed prominence signal [12, 28, 29].

**NAP Citations and Data Consistency**
**Name, Address, and Phone (NAP)** consistency remains a top-five factor for local trust [6, 30, 31]. While traditional directory citations (structured) have seen a relative decline in pack weight (now ~7%), **unstructured citations** (mentions in news, blogs, and "best of" lists) have become the **top three signals for AI search visibility** [2, 17, 32, 33]. Tools like **BrightLocal**, **Moz Local**, **Whitespark**, and **Yext** are standard for managing these listings at scale [34-37].

**Local Landing Pages and Content**
On-page signals account for **15% to 19% of rankings** [1, 2].
*   **Uniqueness Requirement:** Google's 2026 algorithm explicitly penalizes "template clones" where only city names are swapped [17, 38, 39]. Every landing page must include **unique neighborhood references**, local landmarks, and area-specific testimonials [40-42].
*   **Technical Benchmarks:** Pages must hit a **Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) under 2.5s** and an **Interaction to Next Paint (INP) under 200ms** to avoid mobile ranking penalties [43-45].
*   **Schema Markup:** Implementing **LocalBusiness JSON-LD** in the page head is mandatory for entity resolution [46-48].

**Service Area Businesses (SABs)**
SABs without physical storefronts can define up to **20 service areas** [49, 50]. While proximity is a weaker factor for SABs, having a **verified physical address** (even if hidden) is still ranked as the 7th most important individual ranking factor [51, 52]. SABs must compensate for lack of physical proximity by maintaining **higher review velocity** and deeper hyperlocal content [50, 52].

**How AI Search is Changing Discovery**
AI Overviews (AIO) and "AI Mode" now trigger for approximately **25% to 50% of searches**—though sources disagree on the exact saturation (Digital Applied cites ~25% [53], while Oltre AI cites 50%+ [54]). 
*   **Query Fan-Out:** AI engines break one local query into **9–11 sub-queries** (e.g., "parking," "pricing," "reviews") simultaneously [55-57].
*   **Passage Extraction:** Bots like **OAI-SearchBot** and **PerplexityBot** retrieve specific 40–60 word paragraphs rather than whole pages [58-60]. 
*   **Measurement:** On May 13, 2026, **Google Analytics 4** added a native **AI Assistant channel** to track referrals from ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude, though practitioners note this is a "floor" as 60–70% of AI traffic arrives without referrer data [61-63].
